meta.question: When is it safe to treat two different things as the same thing?

groups.title: Core Theory
groups.note: The underlying phenomenon: what structure exists, and what must be preserved for an equivalence to be legitimate at all.

entries.title: The Arithmetic Manifold
entries.summary: The thesis that constraint satisfaction, optimization and physical simulation are projections of one geometric structure, with five proof points: prime-weighted constraints give every clause a unique fingerprint, so none compete for the same gradient signal and the solver stops stalling.

entries.title: The Architecture of Axioms: Geometry, Infinity, and the Prime Code
entries.summary: Axioms are treated as a Boolean lattice whose curvature measures how much each axiom depends on the others. Non-zero curvature is the obstruction to path-independence, and extending the geometry to infinite axiom sets breaks Möbius inversion until primes rescue it.

entries.title: behavioral-quotients
entries.summary: Two computational histories may be equivalent when they produce the same relevant behaviour. This paper states the equivalence relation explicitly, derives which observations must be retained for it to hold, and presents the quotient as a design principle for computation.

entries.title: phantom-clock
entries.summary: Optical phase space becomes a memory medium. Two rays can share a position and still differ in direction and timing, so collapsing them manufactures errors. This essay keeps phase as a first-class coordinate and documents the ellipsoid inside the clock.

entries.title: geometry-of-conditional-logic
entries.summary: Conditionals are given shape. The repository builds a geometry in which if-then-else regions sit at different distances, letting a program ask how two logical situations differ and when they may be treated as interchangeable without changing what the program decides.

entries.title: banzhaf-ensemble-thesis
entries.summary: Game theory meets ensemble learning through Banzhaf power indices, measuring which features shift a model's vote. The thesis asks how much redundancy an ensemble can carry before the extra members change nothing, and how to tell when they already have.

entries.title: TATH
entries.summary: A formal treatment of the laboratory's central device, written as a self-contained document. The definitions are tightened until every later project can be checked against them, including which information an abstraction is allowed to discard and what it must keep.

entries.title: Computation
entries.summary: An essay on computation as the act of discarding what is irrelevant. It works through what computation must retain, what it may forget, and why two questions are inseparable in every system that has to survive contact with a user.

entries.title: Operator Algebra Blogpost
entries.summary: Operator algebra imported as a language for representation: which parts of a system are interchangeable, and what quotient structure survives that interchange. It is the bridge between physics and the abstraction program, and the clearest statement of the shared vocabulary.

entries.title: The Proximity-Identity Functional: Mathematical Foundations of Equilibrium
entries.summary: A mathematical analysis of the proximity-identity functional and its role in determining equilibrium states across physics, machine learning and information theory. The essay derives the functional's fixed points and shows equilibrium as an identity that survives perturbation of the system.

entries.title: The Dynamic Prime Cantor Set: A Fractal Woven from the Primes
entries.summary: A fractal construction on the unit interval built intrinsically from the distribution of prime numbers, replacing the fixed middle-third rule with one driven by prime gaps. The dynamic set is compared against the classical Cantor construction and known fractal dimensions.

entries.title: The Prime Walk: Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking from Number Theory to the Riemann Hypothesis
entries.summary: A random walk on prime powers that connects the molecular Jahn-Teller effect to the Riemann hypothesis through spontaneous symmetry breaking. The walk shows how a physical degeneracy lifts on a number-theoretic landscape, with plots, figures and computed results attached throughout.

entries.title: Multiplicative Archaeology: Recovering Interaction History from Digital Atoms
entries.summary: A framework for treating numbers as structured histories rather than opaque quantities. Digit topology, interaction cost and the archaeology of factorization are used to read a number's past, to say which parts of that past a downstream decision may ignore.

groups.title: Representation / Memory
groups.note: The mirror: the encoding chosen for a system, and how much of it may be discarded before the next decision goes wrong.

entries.title: FUTCache
entries.summary: A bounded-memory sufficient-state representation of explored geometry. FUTCache merges visited states whenever merging loses nothing a later decision needs, scaling to a million production traces while the cache itself stays fixed in size, and released three times in summer 2026.

entries.title: persistent-discovery-index
entries.summary: A microscope for agent behaviour. PDI reads pi, OpenAI, LangSmith and canonical traces to locate the exact boundary where useful discovery ends and wasteful exploration begins, and report that boundary at behavioural resolution instead of returning one blunt aggregate score.

entries.title: novelty-geometry
entries.summary: Traversal, ordered novelty, memory and asymptotic completion in metric and hyperbolic spaces. The framework formalizes which directions an agent has genuinely covered, separating reached territory from a reworded revisit of ground explored, and shows how completion behaves as space grows.

entries.title: model2vec
entries.summary: A fork of the static-embedding toolkit, kept for experiments in compressing models until only the distinctions a downstream decision depends on remain. The fork exists to test how far that compression can be pushed, and where it starts to lose.

entries.title: obs-ai
entries.summary: Obsidian with an AI layer, kept as a knowledge base that can be queried without losing provenance. Notes are indexed so retrieval returns the passage you meant, not the closest wording, and answer can be traced back to its source.

groups.title: Optimization / Search
groups.note: The shadow: behaviour produced by that representation when it meets a hard instance and a deadline.

entries.title: baha
entries.summary: Branch-aware holonomy annealing: when a solver stalls, the escape mechanism detects the fractures where the log-derivative of the partition function diverges and navigates the multi-sheeted analytic surface with Lambert W, cutting complexity from exponential to linear where ordinary annealing stalls.

entries.title: NitroSAT
entries.summary: A powerful linear-time MaxSAT approximator that consistently reaches 99.5 percent satisfaction across graph colouring, clique and Ramsey instances. It prunes aggressively while preserving the distinctions that keep the remaining search honest, and it streams to disk when memory runs short.

entries.title: navokoj
entries.summary: Physics-inspired SAT solving that treats constraints as flowing geometry rather than fixed clauses. The solver navigates the space of partial assignments and learns which regions of it are worth revisiting at all, using spectral information to decide where effort belongs.

entries.title: casimir-sat-solver
entries.summary: Where boolean logic meets quantum mechanics, expressed as a solver whose constraints behave like physical fields settling toward a ground state. The project asks which logical distinctions survive when the clause set is treated as one physical object at once.

entries.title: NoetherLeap
entries.summary: Constraint-aware optimization that pairs physics-informed neural networks with Bayesian search and symmetry discovery. The system exploits conserved quantities to avoid searching dimensions that provably cannot change the outcome, and reports the symmetries it found in advance rather than assuming them.

entries.title: spectral-multiplicative-framework
entries.summary: Graph theory meets quantum mechanics in optimization space, implemented in Crystal for a small executable surface. The framework asks which eigenvalues of a constraint graph a decision can afford to forget, and what breaks when the wrong ones are dropped.

entries.title: How Number Theory Breaks a NP-Hard Problem
entries.summary: An argument that number-theoretic structure can dissolve the apparent hardness of a combinatorial problem rather than merely making it faster. The piece isolates the specific distinction the encoding preserves, and explains why removing that distinction returns the original difficulty unchanged.

entries.title: The Hidden Laws of Imbalance: Advanced Diagnostic Frameworks for Optimization Limits
entries.summary: Diagnostic frameworks for optimisation limits in complex systems, arguing that the right move is often architectural rather than parametric. The essay names the imbalance laws that quietly cap a search, and shows where spending more compute stops helping in practice.

entries.title: Mathematical Mechanism: How the Self-Stabilizing Optimizer Works
entries.summary: Clean, rigorous mathematics behind the exponential-sum manifold and the correlation-based control system applied to NP-hard problems. This is the mechanism write-up: what the solver actually computes, why the correlation term converges, and which guarantees hold for hard instances in practice.

entries.title: The Hidden Manifold Where Geometry Meets Arithmetic: How We Built a Self-Stabilizing Optimizer
entries.summary: Every optimisation problem, from microchip layouts to cloud allocation, is navigation across an energy landscape. This essay describes the system built to stabilise itself there, replacing brute force with a manifold that contracts toward a solution with no human supervision.

entries.title: Probing the Ramsey Limit: Phase Transitions in High-Dimensional Logic
entries.summary: Where perfect solutions become impossible, the constraint system changes character rather than merely getting harder. The essay locates that boundary for high-dimensional logic and reports what survives on the far side of it, where partial satisfaction is all that remains.

entries.title: Navokoj: A Physics Engine for Logic
entries.summary: Boolean logic treated as a continuous dynamical system rather than a search over assignments. The essay argues that constraints can be relaxed as physics, that the relaxation can be computed, and that the result beats classical solvers on industrial instances.

entries.title: Training Dynamics for Discrete Constraint Satisfaction
entries.summary: The parallel between gradient descent through a neural network and continuous optimisation for NP-hard constraint problems, examined directly. The essay asks what a training dynamic looks like when the parameters are clauses, and what a loss surface would even mean.

groups.title: Agents / Authority
groups.note: The shadow for agents: who may ask, who may act, and which distinctions a merge would silently erase.

entries.title: authorization-lattice
entries.summary: Two agents may request the same action while holding entirely different permissions. Ignoring that distinction produces a security failure, so the work orders authority in a lattice and still keeps ownership attached to objects that may have none at all.

entries.title: agent-guardrail
entries.summary: Policy enforcement and permission testing for AI agents. Mock enterprise APIs simulate synthetic user consent, and requests are blocked before deployment when an agent's authority is not actually established, so abstraction never erases the security-relevant distinctions between any two callers.

entries.title: factor-agent
entries.summary: Invariant-preserving agent harnesses built on OTP supervision, arithmetic security lattices and lawful composition. The harness watches that an agent preserves the quantities it was supposed to preserve exactly, and reports every violation rather than silently averaging it out of sight.

entries.title: reify
entries.summary: A declarative SDK and compiler for constraint optimization and decision-intelligence engines. Constraints are declared rather than hand-encoded, and the compiler decides how much structure can be discarded while every remaining degree of freedom still changes the decision that comes out.

entries.title: The Physics-Informed Control Plane for Agentic Systems
entries.summary: Probabilistic agent behaviour turned into reliable, inspectable action through a constraint-governed execution layer. The essay describes the architecture that decides what an agent may do, verifies that it was done, and returns verifiable evidence rather than a promise of compliance.

groups.title: Learning / Physics
groups.note: Where the representation meets physics: multiplicative constraints, operator language, and models that solve for what softmax assumes.

entries.title: eigen-attention
entries.summary: Attention reframed as constrained spectral regression: tokens are eigenvectors under a task-induced operator, and the softmax is solved for rather than assumed. The repository extends the theorem, adds controlled experiments, and ships reproducible checks that show where the approximation holds.

entries.title: multiplicative-pinn-framework
entries.summary: A research framework for solving PDEs with multiplicative constraints, where physics-informed networks are constrained multiplicatively rather than additively. The result preserves positivity and conservation laws that the usual formulation violates, and makes the violation visible whenever it cannot be avoided.

entries.title: Fock Space Computation: A Mathematical Framework for Symbolic Information Processing
entries.summary: A formal demonstration that symbolic computation follows quantum field theory mathematics, with experimental validation in parsing and version control. Fock space supplies the state space, and the framework explains why symbolic systems behave like particle systems under construction and annihilation.

entries.title: A Multiplicative Axis for Constraint Enforcement in Machine Learning
entries.summary: A previously unrecognised axis in loss-design space, built from spectral-multiplicative constraints using analytic number theory and exponential barrier dynamics. The essay shows that constraints can be enforced multiplicatively, preserving properties additive penalties quietly destroy, and explains when this axis helps.

entries.title: The Multiplicative Axis: A New Approach to Navier-Stokes with Prime Number Gates
entries.summary: Additive physics penalties replaced by prime-based multiplicative gates, offering a new perspective on gradient pathology that solvers meet in Navier-Stokes simulation. The essay shows how positivity and conservation laws survive the reformulation that ordinary penalty methods quietly break in practice.

groups.title: Foundations
groups.note: The long-form documents: what the idea is, where it stops, and what it rests on.

entries.title: Unified Mathematical Systems Report
entries.summary: A comprehensive assessment of eight shipped solvers and frameworks sharing one mathematical theory, mapping discrete constraints onto continuous energy landscapes with prime weights and multiplicative dynamics. It reports where the speedups are real, and where they are not at all.

entries.title: Papers and Citations
entries.summary: Every publication with a permanent DOI, plus the theoretical foundations they rest on: Kirkpatrick on annealing, Parisi on spin glasses, Corless on Lambert W, and the statistical-physics literature on thresholds. Written for anyone checking the claims rather than admiring them.

entries.title: Related Work
entries.summary: A measured comparison with simulated annealing, quantum annealing, belief propagation, constraint programming and mixed-integer solvers: what each approach assumes, where it overlaps with the spectral-arithmetic line, and where the difference is a genuine difference in kind rather than in engineering.

entries.title: Where Navokoj Works (and Where It Doesn't)
entries.summary: The scope statement, written before the marketing: NitroSAT is an anytime MaxSAT approximator, strong on structured industrial problems and the wrong tool at the phase transition. Benchmarks are reported against certified optima, with the gaps left visible and honestly named.

entries.title: Glossary
entries.summary: A plain-English reference for every term used across the lab's documentation, from BAHA and phase transitions to prime weighting and the partition function. Each entry links to its deeper explanation, so a reader moves from vocabulary into the argument itself.

entries.title: The Design Philosophy
entries.summary: A working document on running five public surfaces and ten shipped projects without flattening them into one template. The rule is simple: tune every surface to what its reader came to do, and let the surfaces disagree where readers differ.

entries.title: docs
entries.summary: The lab's documentation site, built with Astro: core vision, glossary, concepts, limitations and design philosophy, written so outsiders can follow it. It states the Arithmetic Manifold thesis, cites the evidence ledger, and serves as the front door to the lab.

groups.title: Citable records
groups.note: Every artifact with a permanent identifier — the version of record, not a pointer to one.

entries.title: Solving SAT with Quantum Vacuum Dynamics
entries.summary: Partial assignments are treated as physical microstates in an energy landscape, where almost-satisfying configurations attract one another Casimir-style and coagulate into stable solution clusters. The proposal reframes Boolean satisfiability as a physical process, with the implementation and interactive site attached.

entries.title: Spectral-Multiplicative Optimization Framework
entries.summary: An implementation and validation bundle joining heat-kernel spectral theory to number-theoretic constraint encoding, running at O(nnz) on graphs past a hundred thousand nodes while holding spectral action and multiplicative penalties correlated. It ships diagnostics for inherent optimisation limits baked in.

entries.title: ShunyaBar: Spectral-Arithmetic Phase Transitions for Combinatorial Optimization
entries.summary: The umbrella preprint formalising the solver programme as a spectral triple whose partition function factorises over the adelic ring, with KMS states undergoing a phase transition at inverse temperature one. A renormalisation sweep replaces exponential search with a bounded one.

entries.title: Multiplicative Calculus for Hardness Detection and Branch-Aware Optimization
entries.summary: Hardness is located where the log-derivative of a partition function diverges, because the control parameter there lives on a multi-sheeted analytic surface where optimisers fail. A branch-aware optimiser navigates the sheets with Lambert W, cutting complexity from exponential to linear.

entries.title: NitroSAT: A Physics-Informed MaxSAT Solver Using Heat Kernel Diffusion, Persistent Homology, and Branch-Aware Holonomy Annealing
entries.summary: A MaxSAT solver treating constraint satisfaction as a dynamical system on a clause hypergraph, with heat-kernel smoothing, persistent homology for symmetry detection, zeta-guided resonance injection and branch-aware holonomy annealing. It reaches 99.58 percent satisfaction across 358 instances and nineteen families.

entries.title: Emergent Stochasticity from Serialized Concurrency
entries.summary: Uniform randomness is reconstructed as the invariant measure of a deterministic concurrent system forced through a serialising bottleneck, with the interleaving space written as products of symmetric groups. It is a constructive theory of when distinct histories may be pooled.

entries.title: Novelty Geometry — Initial Release
entries.summary: The frozen first release of the novelty-geometry repository, covering traversal, ordered novelty, memory and asymptotic completion in metric and hyperbolic spaces alike. The record fixes the released version that separates genuinely covered territory from a reworded revisit of ground explored.

entries.title: NoetherLeap — Zenodo software record
entries.summary: The frozen first release of constraint-aware optimization, pairing physics-informed networks with Bayesian search and symmetry discovery. Conserved quantities prune the search space without removing any reachable optimum, and the symmetries are reported rather than simply assumed to hold in advance.

entries.title: Banzhaf Ensemble Thesis
entries.summary: The frozen, citable thesis record of a study of Banzhaf power indices in ensemble learning: which features shift a model's vote, and how much redundancy an ensemble can carry before the extra members change nothing at all in real deployments.

groups.title: Released artifacts
groups.note: Published versions, grouped by project: what froze, and when.

entries.title: FUTCache — v1.3.0, v1.4.0, v.2.0.0
entries.summary: Adaptive semantic cache calibration, then a visit-set representation that scales to a million production traces. The releases measure the same claim from both directions: how much can be merged away, and how little information may be lost while doing it.

entries.title: NitroSAT — v1.0.0, v3.0.0.0, v3.1.0
entries.summary: A production-ready release, followed by a disk-streaming solver that keeps the working set bounded on instances too large for memory. The streaming design is itself an abstraction: only decision-relevant state survives the write, and nothing else is paid for anyway.

entries.title: NoetherLeap — v1.0
entries.summary: The first stable release of constraint-aware optimization, pairing physics-informed networks with Bayesian search and symmetry discovery. Conserved quantities prune the search space without removing any reachable optimum, and the symmetries are reported rather than simply assumed to hold in advance.

entries.title: reify — v0.1.0, v0.2.0
entries.summary: Initial release and first refinement of a declarative SDK for constraint optimization, hosted under the ShunyaBar Labs organisation. Constraints are declared once and the compiler decides what can be safely removed, which is the whole research program in miniature form.

groups.title: Broadcast
groups.note: How the idea becomes reconstructible in someone else's head.

entries.title: Space Time Cafe
entries.summary: An audio notebook following the ideas that became ShunyaBar Labs: primes, invariants, operator theory, geometry, complexity, information, intelligence and mathematical physics. The podcast is the oral prehistory of the lab, recording the conceptual lineage behind the later formal research programme.

entries.title: Shunyabar Labs podcast
entries.summary: The lab's short-form channel: arithmetic rigidity, statistical mechanics for NP-hard search, primes as curvature defects, and demonstrations of the solvers and the constraint engine. Fifteen episodes, ten of them public and available today, each one a piece of the argument.

entries.title: Writing index
entries.summary: Everything written and not promoted into the main index: the concept notes, the research essays and the working blog, with the author's ledes kept intact. Eight pieces are promoted into the research path; the rest stay here, one click away.

groups.title: Elsewhere
groups.note: The lab's other surfaces: notebook, shipping API, evidence ledger, community.

entries.title: Research notebook
entries.summary: The lab notebook: essays sorted into tribes covering core theory, number theory, optimization, with a mindmap of how the projects compose. It is the early face of the work, and says that the entries are exploratory rather than finished proofs.

entries.title: Navokoj
entries.summary: The production solver API behind the lab's work: Navokoj serves MaxSAT over plain HTTP, with proof artifacts you can verify offline and an anytime guarantee that returns the best assignment found. It is the shipping version of the research line.

entries.title: Evidence ledger
entries.summary: A ledger of evidence artifacts: benchmark runs, results and numbers quoted in the papers. It exists so claims can be checked against the runs that produced them, and each figure has somewhere to be traced back to its own source.

entries.title: Lab homepage
entries.summary: The lab's front door: one page stating the thesis, the numbers behind it, and the routes into the solver, the API and the notebook. The shortest path for a visitor who has never heard of the lab and wants more.

entries.title: BAHA beta app
entries.summary: The browser build of the escape mechanism, running the solver in the cloud and showing the branch-aware trajectory as it happens. It is the quickest way to watch the theory work on an instance you care about, without installing anything.

entries.title: SBL community
entries.summary: The community around the lab: a Discord with people working on solvers, constraint systems and the deeper mathematics underneath them. Open questions get posted daily, results get argued about, and the people behind the papers sit in the channel there.

entries.title: Theory portal
entries.summary: The formal architecture of the spectral-arithmetic system, still being written: the axioms, the geometry, the quotient structure and the open questions. It is the deepest door into the lab, and it is currently a placeholder while the proofs are settled.
